macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global stocks edge higher ahead of central-bank decisions
items.summary: U.S. futures were little changed on Tuesday after Wall Street’s tech-led rally, while European shares slipped modestly. Investors are awaiting rate decisions from the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan, all broadly expected to leave rates unchanged.[1][3][7]

items.title: Wall Street rallies on AI optimism
items.summary: The Dow rose 0.52%, the S&P 500 gained 0.96% and the Nasdaq advanced 1.23% in Monday trading, helped by renewed enthusiasm for artificial-intelligence companies and Anthropic’s IPO filing.[6]

items.title: Fed expected to hold rates steady Wednesday
items.summary: Markets broadly expect the Federal Reserve to pause after last month’s rate increase, although elevated inflation expectations have increased pricing for further tightening, including a possible December hike.[1][7]

items.title: HSBC reports strong third-quarter profit
items.summary: HSBC reported third-quarter pretax profit of $9.63 billion, up 32% year over year, maintained its dividend and announced a new share-buyback program.[2]

items.title: Meta expands record AI fundraising plan
items.summary: Meta increased its planned equity fundraising to as much as $97.5 billion to finance artificial-intelligence expansion, while its shares were roughly flat in premarket trading.[7]

items.title: Anthropic files for IPO
items.summary: AI company Anthropic publicly filed plans for a stock-market listing expected in mid-November, reporting sharply higher revenue but also significant losses and disclosed safety risks.[5]

items.title: Whirlpool falls after quarterly loss
items.summary: Whirlpool shares dropped about 8.8% in premarket trading after the appliance maker reported a third-quarter loss and missed revenue expectations.[7]

items.title: Major technology earnings ahead
items.summary: Investors are preparing for results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, with roughly one-third of S&P 500 companies expected to report during the week.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Ripple receives final U.S. approval for national trust bank
items.summary: A U.S. banking regulator approved Ripple National Trust Bank, which will safeguard reserves for the RLUSD stablecoin and custody crypto assets for businesses. The bank will not accept deposits or issue loans.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs post $110 million inflow while Ethereum ETFs see outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $110.34 million in net inflows on October 26, led entirely by BlackRock’s IBIT. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $88.58 million in net outflows, with BlackRock’s ETHA accounting for most of the withdrawals.

items.title: Bitcoin remains near $80,000 ahead of Federal Reserve decision
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $80,238 after dipping near $79,300, while ether was down about 1.4%. Market attention is focused on the Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy decision and the expiration of major Bitcoin options.

items.title: South Korea considers delaying cryptocurrency gains tax until 2029
items.summary: South Korea’s presidential office is reportedly considering a fourth postponement of the country’s 22% cryptocurrency gains tax, which is currently scheduled to begin in January 2027. Parliament would need to amend the law.

items.title: Canada proposes new stablecoin regulations
items.summary: Canada opened a 60-day consultation on draft stablecoin rules that would require non-bank issuers to register with the Bank of Canada, maintain full reserves at Canadian institutions, avoid paying yield to holders, and redeem tokens within three business days.

items.title: Solana Foundation launches institutional delivery-versus-payment standard
items.summary: The Solana Foundation launched Solana DvP, an open-source atomic settlement standard developed with input from JPMorgan, targeting institutional securities and tokenized-asset transactions.

items.title: BlackRock, SBI and Startale work on yen-linked tokenized funds
items.summary: BlackRock joined SBI and Startale in an initiative connecting tokenized investment funds with a yen-denominated stablecoin, expanding institutional experimentation with blockchain-based fund settlement.

items.title: Initia pauses blockchain after token-minting exploit
items.summary: Initia halted its blockchain after a bug reportedly allowed an attacker to mint and transfer approximately $2.7 million worth of tokens. The incident remains under investigation.

items.title: OKX extends funding round at $25 billion valuation
items.summary: Crypto exchange OKX added Circle, Ripple, SC Ventures and QRT as investors in an extension of its funding round, maintaining a reported $25 billion valuation. The OKB token rose about 8%.

items.title: Zcash Foundation says SEC investigation ended without enforcement recommendation
items.summary: The Zcash Foundation announced that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission closed a 2023 investigation into the privacy-focused cryptocurrency without recommending enforcement action.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI announces three AI-generated scientific results
items.summary: OpenAI says its models produced results in mathematics, theoretical physics and computer science, including claims concerning the Kakeya conjecture, Yang–Mills theory and the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The claims are being submitted for expert scrutiny and remain un independently verified.

items.title: Anthropic files for a potential major IPO
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly filed for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. The filing is described as showing rapid revenue growth, substantial losses and a governance structure intended to preserve the company’s safety mission and founder influence.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly releases GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: Reports say OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a lower-cost, faster model aimed at agentic tasks, coding, writing, vision and desktop operation. Availability, pricing and performance claims should be confirmed against official OpenAI documentation.

items.title: Ant Group launches Lingguang 2.0 assistant
items.summary: Ant Group reportedly released Lingguang 2.0, an assistant designed to proactively identify user needs, monitor tasks and send reminders after receiving authorization.

items.title: Hugging Face publishes Carbon-X DNA model
items.summary: Hugging Face reportedly released Carbon-X, an Apache 2.0 model that analyzes raw DNA and responds in English. Early reported benchmark performance places it close to leading general-purpose models, though the figures require independent validation.

items.title: Moonshot AI introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Moonshot AI reportedly launched Kimi K3.1 Pro, claiming a strong position on the Artificial Analysis index and pricing below comparable frontier models. The company says open weights are expected by November 4.

items.title: AI robotics industry approaches a potential inflection point
items.summary: A Nomura report argues that robotics may be approaching a breakthrough driven by improved embodied-AI models, operational data and training feedback loops. The report says current systems remain short of the reliability and manufacturing readiness needed for mass deployment.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Pokémon Unite to shut down in March 2027
items.summary: The Pokémon Company announced that Pokémon Unite will end service on March 23, 2027, concluding roughly six years of operation. The surprise announcement prompted a strong reaction from fans.

items.title: Arkane Lyon given more time to find a buyer
items.summary: Arkane Lyon reportedly faces possible closure unless a buyer or development partner is found, following Microsoft’s restructuring and layoffs. The consultation deadline was extended by one month while options are explored.

items.title: Crimson Desert Enhanced receives major award nominations ahead of DLC
items.summary: Pearl Abyss’s Crimson Desert Enhanced was nominated for Ultimate Game of the Year at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards, adding to nominations for PC Game of the Year and Best Soundtrack. Its first DLC, Unknown Journey, is scheduled for release on October 30.

items.title: Minecraft reportedly launches natively on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Minecraft is reportedly set to receive a native Nintendo Switch 2 release with enhanced visuals and a Super Mario-themed pack. Digital owners are reportedly eligible for the upgrade at no additional cost for a limited period.

items.title: 2XKO adds Sett and Samira in final major update
items.summary: Riot’s fighting game 2XKO reportedly completed its announced roster with the arrival of Sett and Samira on October 27. The update represents the final major roster addition currently planned.

items.title: Pikmin and Pikmin 2 arrive on Android
items.summary: Nintendo reportedly released mobile versions of Pikmin and Pikmin 2 for Android, making both classic games available through a single application.

items.title: Hyphen announced for iOS and Android
items.summary: The precision action-puzzle game Hyphen is scheduled to launch on iPhone, iPad, and Android on October 28. The premium mobile release includes 36 levels and access to community-created levels.
